## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Loka Sutta* (Ud 3.10; PTS Ud 32) is the tenth and final discourse of the *Nandavagga*, the third chapter of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Set shortly after his awakening, the sutta depicts the Buddha contemplating the nature of the world and future rebirth [SuttaCentral]. Its opening narrative framework shares phrasing with other accounts of the post-awakening period, notably the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Māra Saṁyutta* (SN 4), and the *Huṁhuṅka Sutta* (Ud 1.4) [DharmaNexus].
The text is extensively cited and paralleled across early Buddhist and paracanonical literature. Within the Pali tradition, substantial portions of the text (particularly segments §3.1–9.4) are quoted and analyzed in the exegetical treatises *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2 and Pe 8) and *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and commented upon in the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Curated parallels and DharmaNexus alignments agree on cross-language correspondents: passage-level parallels exist in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 32 / UVS 32, *Bhikṣuvarga*, including the Subaši manuscript fragments), Chinese versions of the *Udānavarga* / *Dharmapada* (T 210, T 212, and T 213), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 32), and the *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (San Lo Mvu 64, the Second *Avalokita Sūtra*) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D4054) [DharmaNexus].
No retrieved secondary literature passages discuss Ud 3.10 directly; academic references to a *Loka Sutta* or *Paloka Sutta* typically concern homonymous discourses in the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 112 / AN 4.23) or the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 12.44, SN 35.82).
